q: 按正确顺序排列 system design 面试准备的基础阶段：
steps: 选择一个 delivery framework，作为面试当天的线性路线图
理解 system design interview 到底考什么，可先看 intro 或 mock interview
学习 core concepts、key technologies、common patterns，建立知识地图
why: 先理解面试形态，再选 delivery framework 固定推进顺序，最后补 core concepts 等知识地图；顺序错了容易只背孤立组件。
why_en: Learn the interview format first, then pick a delivery framework, and only then fill in the core-concepts knowledge map.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["1 Intro"] --> B["2 Delivery"]

scenario: 你从没做过 system design interview，连流程和预期都不清楚。
q: 准备的第一步最应该是什么？

先读 intro 或看一次 mock interview
只刷 LeetCode 算法，不看设计内容
直接挑战 ChatGPT 这类最难的题

Read the intro or watch one mock interview first.
Only grind LeetCode algorithm problems.
Jump straight into the hardest problem, like ChatGPT.

why_en: If you have never done a system design interview, learn the format and expectations before memorizing full solutions.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经熟悉面试流程，下一步该练 delivery framework 和刻意练习，而不是重复看 intro。

optionMeanings: 把没读过的完整题解硬背下来。
先看一篇入门介绍或一场示范面试。
只做算法编码练习，不碰架构设计。
从题单里最难的一题开始练手。
optionScenarioImpacts: 没有框架支撑，背的东西很快就忘。
能提前知道面试官会怎么追问、怎么打分。

还没建立基础就先卡在最难的深潜上。
optionDirectness: 不直接：没有基础理解，死记硬背留不住。
最直接：先建立整体画面，才知道要练什么。
不直接：算法和系统设计是两种能力。
不直接：跳过基础会在深潜环节卡死。
optionMeanings_en: Force-memorize solutions you have never studied.
Read a short intro or watch one demo interview first.
Only practice algorithm coding, not architecture.
Start practicing on the hardest problem in the list.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without a framework, memorized answers fade fast.
You learn what interviewers probe and how they grade.
Algorithms help, but they don't close the design gap.
You get stuck on deep dives before building any basics.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: memorizing without understanding does not stick.
Most direct: build the big picture before you know what to practice.
Not direct: algorithms and system design are different skills.
Not direct: skipping basics stalls you at the hardest deep dive.

q: 为什么准备时要选择一个 delivery framework？
options: 它能在快节奏面试里线性推进，避免 scope creep
它能替代所有技术知识，不用再学别的
它保证每道题都有唯一标准答案
它只用来写简历，不在面试时使用
options_en: It keeps you moving linearly in a fast interview and avoids scope creep.
It replaces all the technical knowledge you would otherwise need.
It guarantees every question has one single correct answer.
It is only for writing a resume, not for the actual interview.
why: 系统设计面试时间紧，框架帮你按需求→接口→数据模型→高层设计→深潜推进，没有路线图很容易来回跳。
why_en: A delivery framework gives you a linear roadmap through requirements, API, data model, and deep dives so you don't drift under time pressure.
tradeoff: 固定路线图 vs 自由发挥的即兴设计
optionMeanings: 框架把设计拆成固定阶段，逐步推进。
把框架当成知识库本身。
把框架当成有唯一正确答案的模板。
把框架当成简历工具，不是面试工具。
optionScenarioImpacts: 确保时间紧张时也不漏关键阶段。
没有技术积累，框架也救不了设计。
系统设计通常没有唯一解，这个假设是错的。
面试当天完全用不上，等于没准备框架。
optionDirectness: 最直接：解决的正是时间紧、易跑题的问题。
不直接：框架管路线，不管你会不会技术。
不直接：框架不产生标准答案。
不直接：框架的用途就是面试当天用。
optionMeanings_en: The framework breaks the design into fixed stages.
This treats the framework as the knowledge base itself.
This treats the framework as a template with one right answer.
This treats the framework as a resume tool, not an interview tool.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It keeps you from skipping a key stage under time pressure.
Without technical depth, a framework alone can't save the design.
System design rarely has one correct diagram, so this is wrong.
It would be useless on interview day if that were true.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: it solves exactly the time-pressure, off-track problem.
Not direct: the framework manages pacing, not technical knowledge.
Not direct: a framework does not produce a single standard answer.
Not direct: the whole point is to use it during the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架，如需求→接口→数据模型→高层设计→深潜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when the discussion keeps expanding beyond the core requirements.

q: 文章建议新手先补哪些高层基础材料？（多选）
options: Core Concepts
Key Technologies
Common Patterns

options_en: Core Concepts
Key Technologies
Common Patterns

why: core concepts、key technologies、patterns 是知识地图的骨架，练习题建立在这些可复用概念上，不用每题从零发明。
why_en: Core concepts, key technologies, and common patterns form the reusable knowledge base that practice questions build on.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    K["Knowledge map"] --> C["Core concepts"]
    K --> T["Key technologies"]
    K --> P["Common patterns"]
optionMeanings: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念，例如一致性、缓存。
常用的具体技术组件，例如数据库、消息队列。
反复出现的架构套路，例如读写分离、扇出。
和系统设计练习完全无关的商业信息。
optionScenarioImpacts: 缺了它，做题时不知道用什么概念分析取舍。
缺了它，深潜环节说不出具体组件怎么用。
缺了它，遇到相似场景要重新发明套路。
花时间看股价不会提升任何设计能力。
optionDirectness: 正确：这是知识地图的第一块骨架。
正确：这是具体组件的词汇表。
正确：这是可复用的架构套路库。
错误：这与系统设计练习无关。
optionMeanings_en: Reusable system-design ideas such as consistency and caching.
Concrete components such as databases and message queues.
Recurring architecture strategies such as CQRS or fan-out.
Business trivia with no connection to design practice.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without it, you have no vocabulary for reasoning about tradeoffs.
Without it, you can't name concrete components during a deep dive.
Without it, you reinvent the same pattern every time it shows up.
Reading stock prices builds no design skill at all.
optionDirectness_en: Correct: this is the first pillar of the knowledge map.
Correct: this is the vocabulary of concrete components.
Correct: this is the library of reusable strategies.
Wrong: unrelated to system design practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念，例如一致性、缓存、扩展性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas such as consistency, caching, and scalability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件，例如数据库、消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components such as databases and message queues.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路，例如读写分离、扇出。

q: 文章对“被动看内容”和“实际动手练习”的态度是什么？
options: 被动看内容就够，不用再练习
被动学习有用，但主动做题记得更多
只看答案 key，不用自己设计
练习只适合 senior，新手不用练
options_en: Passive reading alone is enough; no need to practice.
Passive reading helps, but active practice retains far more.
Just read the answer key; you don't need to design it yourself.
Practice is only useful for senior engineers, not beginners.
why: 被动阅读有帮助，但真正动手设计能记得更多；系统设计考的是输出能力，不只是能不能认出正确答案。
why_en: Passive reading helps, but actively designing the system yourself builds far stronger retention and interview performance.
tradeoff: 被动阅读积累认知 vs 主动输出练表达
optionMeanings: 假设读懂等于会讲、会设计。
承认阅读有用，但更看重动手输出。
把看答案当成唯一学习动作。
假设经验决定谁该练习。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试现场要自己组织设计，读懂不等于讲得出。
既保留阅读的输入价值，又补上表达训练。
跳过独立作答，暴露不出自己的真实缺口。
新手恰恰最需要练习来暴露缺口。
optionDirectness: 不直接：忽略了输出能力这个考点。
最直接：兼顾输入与输出两种能力。
不直接：只读答案发现不了自己的漏洞。
不直接：练习价值和资历没有必然关系。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes understanding a solution equals being able to design one.
Accepts reading is useful but values active output more.
Treats reading the answer key as the only study action.
Assumes seniority decides who needs to practice.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: In the real interview you must organize the design yourself.
It keeps the input value of reading and adds output training.
Skipping your own attempt hides your real gaps.
Beginners are exactly who most needs practice to expose gaps.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: it ignores the output skill being tested.
Most direct: it balances input and output skills.
Not direct: reading alone can't reveal your own blind spots.
Not direct: practice value has nothing to do with seniority.

q: 按正确顺序排列一轮推荐的题目练习流程：
steps: 读 requirements，明确要设计什么
自己在 guided practice 或白板上先尝试完整回答
看 answer key，对比自己的设计差距
做几题后找 peer mock，在时间压力下讲出来
why: 先选题、读需求，再自己尝试完整作答，然后对照 answer key 找差距，最后做 peer mock 练时间压力下的表达。
why_en: The loop is choose a question, read the requirements, attempt it yourself, compare against the answer key, and finish with a peer mock.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Q["Pick question"] --> R["Read reqs"]
    R --> S["Solve first"]
    S --> A["Compare answer"]
    A --> M["Peer mock"]
tradeoff: 先自己产出 vs 先看答案抄结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。

scenario: 你刚选了一道 Bitly 题，还没有尝试自己设计，就很想直接看完整题解。
q: 按文章建议，应该怎么做？
options: 直接背下 answer key 的内容
先按需求设计一版，再看 answer key
先读一半 answer key，再接着往下设计
先看架构图，再照着抄一遍设计
options_en: Just memorize the answer key directly.
Design your own version first, then read the answer key.
Read half the answer key, then design the rest yourself.
Look at the diagram first, then copy the design from it.
why: 先自己尝试才会暴露真实缺口：需求漏项、接口不清、深潜没展开；直接看答案容易产生“我懂了”的错觉。
why_en: Trying the design yourself first exposes real gaps that reading the answer key directly would hide.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是想快速预览题目范围，可以先粗看目录；真正训练输出能力时必须先独立作答。
tradeoff: 先自己产出暴露缺口 vs 先读答案获得结构感
optionMeanings: 把答案当成要记住的正确文本。
先独立设计，把答案当对照而不是起点。
看了一半就带着答案的思路往下补。
把画图这一步换成照抄现成的图。
optionScenarioImpacts: 背下来的是别人的结构，不是你的判断。
能看清自己漏了哪条需求、哪个深潜。
后半段其实被答案带着走，不算独立完成。
省掉了自己组织架构的练习，只剩临摹。
optionDirectness: 不直接：产生“看懂了”的错觉。
最直接：暴露真实差距，正是练习的目的。
不直接：一半独立一半抄，缺口照样藏起来。
不直接：临摹图纸练不到设计判断。
optionMeanings_en: Treat the answer key as text to be memorized.
Design independently first, using the answer only as a reference.
Read half, then let the answer's logic guide the rest.
Replace the sketching step with copying an existing diagram.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: What you memorize is someone else's structure, not your judgment.
You can see exactly which requirement or deep dive you missed.
The second half is really guided by the answer, not truly independent.
You skip organizing the architecture yourself and just trace it.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: it creates a false sense of understanding.
Most direct: exposing real gaps is the whole point of practice.
Not direct: half-independent still hides the same gaps.
Not direct: tracing a diagram doesn't train design judgment.

q: 文章建议自己练习时可以使用什么工具或形式？

只写出最终的数据库 schema
用 Guided Practice 或虚拟白板

Only write out the final database schema.

optionMeanings: 把设计过程留在脑子里，不外化。
只产出最终结果，跳过设计过程。
用带反馈的引导工具或绘图白板动手练。
把练习简化成背名词。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官看不到你的思考过程，没法评分。

最直接：练的正是结构化输出这项能力。
不直接：背名词不是设计能力。
optionMeanings_en: Keep the whole design process in your head, never externalized.
Only produce the final result, skipping the design process.
Practice hands-on with a feedback tool or a drawing whiteboard.
Reduce practice to memorizing terminology.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: An interviewer can't see or grade a thought process that stays in your head.
It skips the part where you show your tradeoffs.
It forces you to explicitly lay out requirements, components, and data flow.
Knowing terms is not the same as using them to design.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: there is zero externalized practice effect.
Not direct: a schema is only a small slice of the design.
Most direct: it trains exactly the structured-output skill being tested.
Not direct: memorizing terms is not a design skill.

scenario: 你刚开始练 system design，想选择第一批题来建立信心和基本套路。
q: 更合理的选择是什么？
options: 直接从 Google Docs、Payment System、ChatGPT 开始
从 Bitly、Dropbox、News Aggregator 等 easy 题开始
只看 More Practice 里没有 write-up 的题
不选题，直接做 mock
options_en: Jump straight into Google Docs, Payment System, and ChatGPT.
Start with easy problems such as Bitly, Dropbox, and News Aggregator.
Only use More Practice problems that have no write-up.
Skip picking a problem and go straight to a mock.
why: 新手先用 easy 题训练框架和基本组件选择，再逐步上 medium/hard；过早做 hard 题容易误判为“系统设计太难”。
why_en: Beginners should start with easy problems to build the delivery framework before moving into harder designs.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已有大量系统设计经验，可以直接用 medium/hard 题查漏补缺。
tradeoff: 先易后难打基础 vs 直接挑战高难度题
optionMeanings: 从高难度题直接入手。
从简单题练框架和基本选型判断。
只用没有书面题解的补充题库。
跳过练题环节，直接进模拟面试。
optionScenarioImpacts: 容易同时卡在框架不熟和约束太多两件事上。
能在低复杂度下把框架用顺，再叠加难度。
没有答案对照，新手更难发现自己的缺口。
没有练过框架，mock 时会漏步骤、答不完整。
optionDirectness: 不直接：难度和陌生框架叠加，挫败感强。
最直接：符合新手先建立信心的目标。
不直接：缺参照物，不利于新手起步。
不直接：跳过了练框架这一步。

Start with easy problems to practice the framework and basic choices.
Only use extra problems that have no written solution.
Skip practicing problems and go straight to a mock.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You get stuck on an unfamiliar framework and heavy constraints at once.
You can get comfortable with the framework before adding difficulty.
With no reference solution, beginners struggle to spot their own gaps.
Without framework practice, the mock will miss steps and feel incomplete.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: stacking difficulty on an unfamiliar framework is discouraging.
Most direct: it matches the beginner's goal of building confidence.
Not direct: no reference point makes it hard for beginners to start.
Not direct: it skips the framework-practice step entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

scenario: 你在 HelloInterview 的题单里发现，一部分题在正文 common questions，另一部分只出现在 More Practice 区。

options: More Practice 里的题全部是 easy 难度
Common questions 完全不能用来练习
只有 Common questions 附带 write-up
两个题单在内容和形式上完全没有差别
options_en: Every problem in More Practice is easy difficulty.
Common questions cannot be used for practice at all.
Only common questions come with a write-up.
The two lists have no difference in content or format.
why: 正文题单带书面题解，是主线练习材料；More Practice 是补充题库，强调引导练习和 AI 反馈，不一定有完整文章。
why_en: Common questions include a written guide, while More Practice adds extra guided problems that may not have a full write-up.
tradeoff: 带书面题解的主线材料 vs 靠引导反馈的补充题库
optionMeanings: 把区别错误归因为难度分布。
把区别错误归因为能不能练习。
两个题单在“是否配书面题解”上不同。
否认两个题单存在结构差异。
optionScenarioImpacts: 两个题单其实都横跨 easy 到 hard。
两个题单都能拿来做 guided practice。
决定你该先读文章还是直接上手引导练习。
会让你误用某个题单的学习方式。
optionDirectness: 不直接：难度分布不是区分它们的维度。
不直接：两个题单都能练习，只是形式不同。
最直接：准确指出两者的结构差异。
不直接：结构差异真实存在。
optionMeanings_en: Misattributes the difference to difficulty distribution.
Misattributes the difference to whether practice is possible.
The two lists differ in whether a written solution exists.
Denies that a structural difference exists.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Both lists actually span easy through hard.
Both lists support guided practice either way.
It decides whether you read an article first or jump into guided practice.
It leads you to misuse one of the two lists.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: difficulty distribution is not what separates them.
Not direct: both lists can be practiced, just in different forms.
Most direct: it names the actual structural difference.
Not direct: a real structural difference does exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 题目附带的完整书面题解文章。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-up is the full written solution article that comes with a question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分步骤引导、边做边给反馈的练习工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 练习过程中由 AI 即时给出的评价和建议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI feedback is real-time evaluation and suggestions generated during practice.

scenario: 你已经能独立完成 Bitly 和 Dropbox，但 medium 题会卡在深潜和 tradeoff。
q: 下一步最合理的练习目标是什么？
options: 换 Ticketmaster、Tinder 这类 medium 题练深潜
回头重新只看 intro 入门介绍文章
跳过 medium，直接冲 ChatGPT 这类 hard 题
感觉太难，直接停止刷题练习
options_en: Move to medium problems like Ticketmaster and Tinder to practice deep dives.
Go back to only reading the intro article.
Skip medium and jump straight to a hard problem like ChatGPT.
Feel discouraged and stop practicing altogether.
why: 难度要逐步递进：easy 建框架，medium 练真实 tradeoff，hard 再练复杂约束。
why_en: A good progression moves from easy framework practice into medium tradeoffs before tackling hard production complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果连 easy 题都讲不完整，应先继续打磨框架，而不是急着升级难度。
tradeoff: 循序渐进升级难度 vs 跳级挑战更难的题
optionMeanings: 用中等难度题练需求到深潜的过渡。
退回最基础的入门材料。
跳过中间难度直接挑战最难题。
把卡壳当成停止的理由。
optionScenarioImpacts: 正好对上“卡在深潜和 tradeoff”这个具体缺口。
已经会框架了，重看 intro 补不上深潜缺口。
缺口还没补，hard 题会叠加更多复杂约束。
缺口永远得不到练习机会。
optionDirectness: 最直接：针对性补上深潜和取舍的短板。
不直接：intro 讲的是形式，不是深潜技巧。
不直接：难度跳级会同时暴露多个缺口。
不直接：停止练习解决不了任何缺口。
optionMeanings_en: Use medium-difficulty problems to practice the deep-dive transition.
Retreat to the most basic introductory material.
Skip the middle tier and jump to the hardest problems.
Treat getting stuck as a reason to quit.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It targets exactly the deep-dive and tradeoff gap described.
You already know the framework; the intro won't fix deep-dive gaps.
The gap is still open, and hard problems stack even more constraints.
The gap never gets a chance to close.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: it targets the deep-dive and tradeoff weakness directly.
Not direct: the intro covers format, not deep-dive technique.
Not direct: jumping difficulty exposes multiple gaps at once.
Not direct: stopping fixes none of the underlying gaps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 针对某个组件或场景做更细的设计展开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is a detailed exploration of one component or scenario in the design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tradeoff is the balance you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全练习系统设计题的关键规则：
text: 先{{自己尝试}}，再看{{answer key}}；最后通过{{peer mock}}训练在时间压力下讲出设计。
why: 这条规则把输入学习变成输出训练：先产出，再对照，最后计时讲出来，三步都不能跳。
why_en: The rule turns passive input into active output: attempt first, compare against the answer, then rehearse it under time pressure.
tradeoff: 先产出后对照 vs 先看答案后模仿

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

scenario: 你把某道题的 answer key 从头读到尾，觉得完全看懂了，但没有自己动手画过。
q: 只看题解、不自己画设计，最容易造成什么问题？
options: 自动获得口头表达能力
自动知道所有 tradeoff
面试时完全不需要澄清需求
产生“看懂了”等于“会讲会设计”的错觉
options_en: You automatically gain verbal explanation skills.
You automatically know every tradeoff involved.
You no longer need to clarify requirements in the interview.
You get the illusion that understanding equals being able to design and explain it.
why: 阅读答案时结构和取舍已经被作者组织好了；面试现场你必须自己组织，这是两种不同能力。
why_en: Reading a solution can create a false sense of mastery because the author already organized the structure and tradeoffs for you.
optionMeanings: 假设阅读自动训练口头表达。
假设阅读自动覆盖所有取舍场景。
假设阅读能替代需求澄清练习。
把“读懂”错当成“能独立复现”。
optionScenarioImpacts: 表达能力要靠开口讲才能训练，阅读练不到。
换个约束，取舍就会不同，阅读记不住所有变体。
澄清需求是主动提问的技能，读答案不涉及。
面试现场要自己搭结构，读的时候没练过这步。
optionDirectness: 不直接：表达能力靠开口练，不是靠读。
不直接：tradeoff 因场景而变，读不出全部。
不直接：澄清需求是独立的主动技能。
最直接：这正是被动阅读最容易踩的坑。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes reading automatically trains verbal explanation.
Assumes reading automatically covers every tradeoff scenario.
Assumes reading replaces the skill of clarifying requirements.
Mistakes 'I understood it' for 'I can reproduce it myself.'
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Speaking skill only grows by speaking out loud, not by reading.
Change the constraint and the tradeoff changes; reading can't cover every variant.
Clarifying requirements is an active questioning skill reading doesn't touch.
In the real interview you must build the structure yourself, a step reading skips.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: speaking skill is trained by speaking, not reading.
Not direct: tradeoffs shift with scenario; reading can't cover them all.
Not direct: clarifying requirements is a separate, active skill.
Most direct: this is exactly the trap passive reading falls into.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

scenario: 你练题时经常一会儿讲数据库、一会儿讲缓存、一会儿又回到需求，最后时间不够。
q: 最直接的修正是什么？
options: 继续想到哪讲到哪，不用框架
只画最终架构图，跳过前面阶段
固定用 delivery framework，按阶段控制范围
跳过 requirements，直接讲架构
options_en: Keep improvising, jumping topics without a framework.
Only draw the final architecture diagram, skip earlier stages.
Commit to a delivery framework and control scope stage by stage.
Skip requirements and jump straight into architecture.
why: 框架的价值就是让你线性推进、防止 scope creep；系统设计是逐步收敛问题，不是脑暴组件。
why_en: A delivery framework keeps your answer linear and prevents scope creep during a fast-paced interview.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经能自然组织答案，框架可以隐藏在表达里；但练习阶段仍应显式使用它。
tradeoff: 固定阶段推进 vs 想到哪讲到哪
optionMeanings: 让讨论顺序完全跟着联想走。
把设计压缩成只剩最终结果。
用固定阶段顺序逼自己不跑题。
跳过需求，直接从组件开始想。
optionScenarioImpacts: 正是这种跳跃导致时间不够用完。
没有前面阶段支撑，架构图也讲不清为什么这么画。
每个阶段有时间边界，跳来跳去的问题被结构消除。
没有需求锚点，很容易设计出偏题的系统。
optionDirectness: 不直接：这正是当前问题的根源，不是修正。
不直接：缺前面阶段，架构图站不住脚。
最直接：结构本身就是在解决“跳来跳去”的问题。
不直接：需求是后续所有阶段的锚点。
optionMeanings_en: Let the discussion order follow free association.
Compress the design down to just the final result.
Use a fixed stage order to force yourself to stay on track.
Skip requirements and start thinking from components.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This jumping is exactly what is eating your time now.
Without earlier stages, you can't justify why the diagram looks that way.
Each stage has a time boundary, so the jumping-around problem is structurally removed.
Without a requirements anchor, it's easy to design the wrong system.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: this is the root cause, not a fix.
Not direct: without earlier stages, the diagram has no justification.
Most direct: the structure itself solves the jumping-around problem.
Not direct: requirements anchor every later stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试开始时明确的功能性和非功能性需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements are the functional and non-functional constraints you clarify at the start.

q: 先读 Core Concepts / Key Technologies / Patterns 的收益是什么？（多选）
options: 知道系统设计题常见组件和模式的边界
做题时能复用已有概念，而不是每题从零发明
帮助建立学习范围
保证不用再练任何题
options_en: You learn the boundaries of common components and patterns.
You can reuse existing concepts instead of reinventing them each time.
It helps you scope what you need to study.
It guarantees you never have to practice a question.
why: 基础材料不是替代练题，而是给练题提供词汇和取舍框架；没有基础，题解容易变成死记硬背。
why_en: The foundations give you reusable vocabulary and a tradeoff framework, but they do not replace active practice.
optionMeanings: 了解常见组件/模式各自适用的边界。
把学过的概念当工具直接复用。
明确该学到多深、多广。
假设读完基础就不用再练题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 遇到新题能快速判断该用哪类组件。
省去每题重新发明轮子的时间。
避免漫无目的地乱看资料。
会让你误以为可以跳过输出训练。
optionDirectness: 正确：这是阅读基础材料最直接的收获。
正确：这是复用能力的来源。
正确：这是范围管理的收益。
错误：基础材料不能替代练题。
optionMeanings_en: You learn where each common component or pattern applies.
You reuse concepts you've already learned as tools.
It clarifies how deep and how broad to study.
It assumes finishing the foundations means skipping practice.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You can quickly judge which component fits a new problem.
It saves you from reinventing the wheel on every question.
It keeps you from wandering aimlessly through material.
It falsely suggests you can skip output training.
optionDirectness_en: Correct: this is the most direct payoff of reading the foundations.
Correct: this is where reuse ability comes from.
Correct: this is the scoping benefit.
Wrong: foundations cannot replace active practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

scenario: 你已经练过几道题，准备进入 mock 阶段，想让反馈更贴近目标面试。
q: peer mock 对象怎么选更好？
options: 只找完全不了解 system design 的人
优先找目标公司或相近风格的工程师
只对着镜子读答案
只用随机题目生成器，不要反馈
options_en: Find someone with no system design background at all.
Prioritize an engineer from the target company or a similar interview style.
Just read the answer out loud to a mirror.
Use a random question generator with no feedback.
why: 目标公司员工更熟悉该公司的面试节奏和评价偏好；反馈越贴近目标环境，练习价值越高。
why_en: A peer from the target company is more likely to give feedback aligned with that company's interview style.
whenOtherWins: 找不到目标公司的人时，找有系统设计面试经验的工程师，重点是拿到真实追问。
tradeoff: 贴近目标公司的真实反馈 vs 容易约到的泛泛反馈
optionMeanings: 找完全没有相关背景的人陪练。
找了解目标评分标准的人给反馈。
自己对自己复述，没有外部反馈。
只刷题，主动放弃反馈环节。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方提不出有价值的技术追问。
追问方式和评分口味更接近真实面试官。
没有人能指出你漏掉的需求或取舍。
没有反馈就发现不了自己的盲点。
optionDirectness: 不直接：缺乏专业追问，练习价值有限。

不直接：反馈环节被主动砍掉了。
optionMeanings_en: Pair with someone who has no relevant background at all.
Find someone who knows the target grading style to give feedback.
Recite your own answer to yourself, with no outside feedback.
Only drill questions and deliberately skip the feedback step.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They can't ask technically meaningful follow-up questions.
Follow-up questions and grading feel closer to the real interviewer.
No one can point out the requirement or tradeoff you missed.
Without feedback, your blind spots stay hidden.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: lacking expert follow-up limits the practice value.
Most direct: feedback quality is what determines a mock's value.
Not direct: this isn't really a mock at all.
Not direct: it deliberately removes the feedback step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

q: “读懂题解”和“面试中讲出设计”的最大区别是什么？
options: 讲出设计要在时间压力下自己组织结构和取舍
读懂题解更难，因为不需要表达
两者完全一样
讲出设计不需要任何技术判断
options_en: Explaining a design out loud means organizing structure and tradeoffs yourself, under time pressure.
Reading a write-up is harder because it requires no explanation.
The two are exactly the same skill.
Explaining a design requires no technical judgment at all.
why: 面试是实时沟通：要澄清需求、排序问题、画图、解释取舍并响应追问；阅读只是输入的一部分。
why_en: Speaking a design out loud requires actively organizing structure, tradeoffs, and communication under time pressure.
tradeoff: 主动组织表达 vs 被动接收阅读
optionMeanings: 把讲设计当成主动输出加沟通的任务。
颠倒了阅读和表达的难度关系。
否认输入和输出是两种技能。
错误地剥离了技术判断这一核心。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对应面试官真正在评估的能力。
表达通常比阅读更难，不是更容易。
会让人误以为看懂题解就等于会面试。
面试恰恰全程都在考技术判断。
optionDirectness: 最直接：准确指出两者的核心差异。
不直接：难度方向说反了。
不直接：两种技能的考察方式完全不同。
不直接：技术判断正是核心考点。
optionMeanings_en: Treats explaining a design as active output plus communication.
Reverses the actual difficulty relationship between reading and speaking.
Denies that input and output are different skills.
Incorrectly strips out technical judgment as the core.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It matches what the interviewer is actually evaluating.
Speaking is usually harder than reading, not easier.
It wrongly implies understanding a write-up equals being interview-ready.
Technical judgment is exactly what's being tested throughout.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: it names the real core difference.
Not direct: the difficulty direction is backwards.
Not direct: the two skills are assessed completely differently.
Not direct: technical judgment is the core of the interview.

scenario: 主线 common questions 题单大约有 30 道，分布在 easy（约 4 道）、medium（约 13 道）、hard（约 13 道）三档。
q: 这个题量和难度分布，最支持哪条备考策略？
options: 跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard
题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上
只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题
在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档
options_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
why: 约 30 道题在三档间分布均衡，说明常见面试难度本身就是均衡分布的；两周内做不完全部，应按难度分层抽样，而不是只啃一档或反复刷同一批题。
why_en: With about thirty problems split evenly across easy, medium, and hard, the right move in a short window is to sample every tier, not just one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文章正文列出的主线练习题单，带书面 write-up。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common questions are the main practice list in the article, each with a written guide.

scenario: 你独立完成一题后，对比 answer key 发现自己的高层架构不同。

options: 直接把自己写的完整答案删除重做一遍

跳过复盘环节，直接进入下一道练习题
比较背后的 requirements 和 tradeoffs
options_en: Delete your own complete answer and redo it from scratch.
Only check whether the component names on both sides match.
Skip the review step and go straight to the next practice question.
Compare the requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference.
why: 系统设计通常没有唯一图；复盘要找出作者为什么选了某个组件、你漏了哪个约束、哪些取舍没讲清。
why_en: The useful review compares requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference, not the memorization of one architecture diagram.
whenOtherWins: 如果你的方案违反了硬性需求或指标，那不是风格差异，是需要修正的设计错误。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Mine["My design"] --> Gap["Find gaps"]
    Key["Answer key"] --> Gap
    Gap --> Req["Requirements"]
    Gap --> Trade["Tradeoffs"]
    Gap --> Deep["Deep dives"]
tradeoff: 复盘约束和取舍 vs 复盘表面架构图
optionMeanings: 把不同结果当成完全失败处理。
只核对名词，不核对决策依据。
放弃从这道题里学习的机会。
把差异当成理解取舍的线索去追问。
optionScenarioImpacts: 丢掉了本可以对比学习的素材。
组件名一样，决策逻辑可能完全没学到。
同样的缺口会在下一题重复出现。
能定位自己漏掉的约束或没考虑的取舍。
optionDirectness: 不直接：删掉答案不等于理解了差距。
不直接：名称一致不代表理解一致。
不直接：跳过复盘等于放弃反馈环节。
最直接：直接命中“差异从哪来”这个问题。
optionMeanings_en: Treat a different result as total failure.
Only check naming, not the reasoning behind decisions.
Give up the chance to learn from this question.
Treat the difference as a clue to chase down the reasoning.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You throw away material you could have learned from.
Matching names doesn't mean you learned the decision logic.
The same gap will resurface on the next question.
You can pinpoint the missed constraint or unconsidered tradeoff.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: deleting the answer doesn't build understanding.
Not direct: matching names doesn't mean matching reasoning.
Not direct: skipping review throws away the feedback step.
Most direct: it goes straight at where the difference came from.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 设计必须满足的硬性限制条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraints are the hard limits a design must satisfy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tradeoffs are the balances you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全准备路线的三个基础动作：
text: 理解{{system design interview}}是什么，选择{{Delivery Framework}}，再学习{{Core Concepts}}、{{Key Technologies}}和{{Common Patterns}}。
why: 三步构成从面试形态到表达框架、再到知识地图的基础路线；缺一步，后面练习容易失焦。
why_en: The foundation is understanding the interview format, choosing a delivery framework, and then filling in core concepts, technologies, and patterns.
tradeoff: 先搭完整基础 vs 边练边补概念

scenario: 你没有练习伙伴，但想先自己模拟白板设计流程。
q: 文章建议的可行替代是什么？
options: 什么都不做，干等 mock 机会
只截图收藏别人的答案
用 Guided Practice 或白板自己讲一遍
只写代码，跳过架构图
options_en: Do nothing and just wait for a mock opportunity.
Only screenshot and save other people's answers.
Use Guided Practice or a whiteboard to narrate it yourself.
Only write code, skip the architecture diagram.
why: 没有 peer 时也能用 guided practice 或白板练结构化输出；重点是不要停留在只读的模式。
why_en: Guided practice or a virtual whiteboard lets you practice structured output even before you find a mock partner.
whenOtherWins: 能独立讲完整后，仍应尽快找 mock，因为真实追问很难自我模拟。
tradeoff: 自己动手画讲 vs 被动等待搭子
optionMeanings: 把练习进度完全交给等待。
把收集答案当成练习本身。
自己扮演讲解者，边画边说完整流程。
把练习范围缩小到只剩代码。
optionScenarioImpacts: 找到搭子前的时间完全被浪费。
截图不会训练任何表达或设计能力。
没有搭子也能练到结构化输出这一步。
漏掉了需求、架构和取舍的练习。
optionDirectness: 不直接：等待不是一种练习方式。
不直接：收藏答案不产生任何输出练习。
最直接：正是文章给出的替代方案。
不直接：代码只是设计的最后一步。
optionMeanings_en: Hand all your practice progress over to waiting.
Treat collecting answers as practice itself.
Play the role of the presenter, drawing and narrating the full flow.
Shrink the scope of practice down to just code.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The time before finding a partner is completely wasted.
Screenshots train no explanation or design skill.
You can still practice structured output without a partner.
It skips practicing requirements, architecture, and tradeoffs.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: waiting is not a form of practice.
Not direct: collecting answers produces no output practice.
Most direct: this is exactly the alternative the article suggests.
Not direct: code is only the last step of the design.

termDefinitions.meaning: HelloInterview 提供的分步骤引导式练习工具，边做边给反馈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided Practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

scenario: 你在练题时没有固定推进顺序，想到哪讲到哪。
q: 没有清晰 roadmap 的系统设计回答最容易出现什么问题？
options: 所有问题都会自动收敛，不用管
已经不再需要澄清任何需求
即兴发挥必然比用框架更快
scope creep：不断发散、偏离核心需求
options_en: All problems automatically converge on their own, no effort needed.
You no longer need to clarify any requirements at all.
Improvising is guaranteed to be faster than using a framework.
Scope creep: the discussion keeps drifting away from core requirements.
why: 面试时间有限，发散会吃掉高层设计和关键深潜的时间；框架的作用就是让你知道下一步该讲什么。
why_en: Without a roadmap, answers tend to drift into scope creep and lose time needed for the core design.
optionMeanings: 假设无框架也能自动聚焦。
假设可以跳过需求澄清环节。
假设即兴发挥天然更省时间。
讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求。
optionScenarioImpacts: 现实中恰恰相反，没框架更容易发散。
没澄清需求，设计方向可能整体跑偏。
来回摸索方向反而更费时间。
高层设计和深潜的时间被无关话题占用。
optionDirectness: 不直接：与常见的真实结果相反。
不直接：需求澄清和框架无关，一直需要。
不直接：即兴发挥通常更慢，不是更快。
最直接：这是缺框架最典型的后果。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes discussions self-focus even without a framework.
Assumes you can skip the requirements-clarification step.
Assumes improvising is inherently faster.
The discussion keeps expanding away from the core requirements.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: In reality the opposite happens without a framework.
Without clarifying requirements, the whole design can drift off target.
Wandering back and forth actually costs more time.
Time meant for the high-level design and deep dives gets eaten by tangents.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: opposite of what typically happens.
Not direct: clarifying requirements is unrelated to framework and always needed.
Not direct: improvising is usually slower, not faster.
Most direct: this is the textbook consequence of lacking a roadmap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when the discussion keeps expanding beyond the core requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试回答时预先规划好的阶段顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A roadmap is the pre-planned sequence of stages for answering the interview.

scenario: 你只有两周准备系统设计，基础薄弱，但每天能练习。
q: 最合理的时间分配倾向是什么？
options: 快速过基础，再用 easy/medium 题主动输出
两周全部用来看题解，不做输出
只做 hard 题，不补基础
只背技术名词列表
options_en: Skim the foundations fast, then drill active output on easy/medium problems.
Spend the full two weeks only reading write-ups, no output.
Only do hard problems, skip the foundations.
Only memorize a list of technical terms.
why: 短期备考要先建最低可用框架，再尽快进入输出练习；短板通常在讲题过程中才暴露。
why_en: With limited time, build the minimum framework quickly and spend most effort on active easy-to-medium practice.
whenOtherWins: 如果基础已经扎实，可以把更多时间投入 hard 题 mock 和深潜复盘。
tradeoff: 快速搭框架转向输出 vs 长时间只做输入阅读
optionMeanings: 把有限时间优先分给动手输出。
把所有时间都花在被动阅读上。
跳过基础，直接冲最难题目。
把练习简化成背名词。
optionScenarioImpacts: 两周内既补了基础缺口，又练到了表达。
面试现场的表达短板完全没被暴露过。
基础不牢，hard 题的复杂约束会全部卡壳。
背下名词不等于会用它们做设计判断。
optionDirectness: 最直接：匹配“时间少、基础弱”这个具体约束。
不直接：两周里最稀缺的输出练习被完全放弃。
不直接：基础缺口没补，hard 题只会更挫败。
不直接：名词不是可以直接使用的设计能力。
optionMeanings_en: Prioritize the limited time toward hands-on output.
Spend all the time on passive reading.
Skip the foundations and rush straight to the hardest problems.
Reduce practice to memorizing terminology.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: In two weeks you close the foundation gap and get output practice.
The output weakness that shows up in the real interview never gets exposed.
Without a solid foundation, hard-problem constraints will stall you.
Memorizing terms is not the same as using them to make design calls.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: it matches the specific constraint of little time and weak basics.
Not direct: it gives up the output practice that's scarcest in two weeks.
Not direct: skipping the foundation only makes hard problems more frustrating.
Not direct: terms are not a usable design skill by themselves.

q: 按正确顺序排列一条完整的准备路线：
steps: 做 peer mock，训练在时间压力下沟通

why: 完整路线是先知道怎么答，再补概念词汇，然后靠做题输出，最后用 mock 逼近真实面试。
